inventory.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
inventory.visualPurpose: The AUC (plasma concentration vs time) plot
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: The AUC plot: plasma concentration on the Y-axis against time on the X-axis, two curves drawn — the IV curve (higher, peaking immediately) labeled AUCIV, and the oral curve (lower, peaking later) labeled AUCOral — illustrating the bioavailability concept; the bioavailability formula F = [AUCoral × DoseIV] / [Doseoral × AUCIV] × 100 printed beside the plot. A vector figure (no raster).
inventory.kypLocation: the registry visual (the top-left panel of the PharmacokineticsMap)

inventory.sourceFigureDescription: The Vd compartment / drug-types table: rows = Low, Medium, High Vd; columns = Compartment (Intravascular, ECF, All tissues including fat), Drug types (Large/charged molecules; plasma protein bound, Small hydrophilic molecules, Small lipophilic molecules especially if bound to tissue protein). Pure text, no figures.

inventory.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
inventory.visualPurpose: The age-related PK changes (Absorption / Distribution / Metabolism / Excretion)
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: The age-related PK changes: a four-row bulleted list comparing elderly vs young — Absorption (mostly unaffected), Distribution (↓ total body water → ↓ Vd of hydrophilic drugs; ↑ total body fat → ↑ Vd of lipophilic drugs), Metabolism (↓ hepatic mass and blood flow → ↓ first-pass metabolism; Phase I decreased, Phase II preserved), Excretion (↓ renal mass and blood flow → ↓ GFR → ↓ renal clearance). Pure text, no figures.
inventory.kypLocation: the registry visual (the age-related PK strip inside the PharmacokineticsMap) + the rapid-review section in the note
